I have viewed one reference image for Anthracnose and one for Cigar End Rot.

The Anthracnose reference image (`PlantWild_26.jpg`) shows ripe bananas with extensive dark brown to black lesions, which are somewhat sunken. This matches the description of Anthracnose quite well, and also bears a strong resemblance to the test image, particularly the yellow/orange banana.

The Cigar End Rot reference image (`PlantWild_30.jpg`) shows a green banana with a very distinct blackened, shriveled, and dry rot at the blossom end, resembling a cigar ash. While the test image has blackening at the ends, it doesn't have the same "cigar end" appearance with powdery grey conidia. The blackening in the test image is more distributed and less focused on a very specific shriveled tip.

At this point, Anthracnose seems like a stronger candidate based on visual similarity. I will continue to explore other classes, but my budget for reference images is exactly 8. I have used 2. I need to view 6 more images from at least 5 other distinct classes.

I will view one image from each of the remaining 5 classes that affect either the leaf or whole plant, to ensure I'm not missing any other possibilities, even though my initial assessment points to a fruit disease. I should prioritize classes that have more generic symptoms.
